source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Inspect the brakes meticulously by applying consistent pressure while the vehicle is securely raised or on a lift to prevent accidents.

3. Use a manufacturer-recommended brake testing gauge or device to measure the pressure applied and travel distance of the brake pedal for standardized results.

4. Visually inspect the brake components, including pads, discs, calipers, brake lines, and fluid levels. Note any abnormalities such as excessive wear, signs of leakage, or physical damage.

5. Record the condition of each brake component in the inspection report. Use a detailed checklist to ensure all components are evaluated.

6. Test the parking/emergency brake to determine if it holds the vehicle securely on an incline.

7. Perform a road test under controlled conditions to evaluate brake effectiveness and responsiveness. Note any delays in stopping distance, pulling to one side, or overheating symptoms.

8. For vehicles equipped with Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS), perform additional tests to ensure the system engages and
